I am an old woman with a small piece of land here in the South South, and I plant my yam and cassava like my mother taught me. I cannot afford the chemical fertilizer from the market, and it is far to travel — I will use the droppings from my goats and the ash from cooking to feed the soil. The seeds I keep from last year's harvest are good enough; I do not need those new ones from the agro-dealer. The rain here is plenty, so I do not worry about water, and I will do the work myself with help from my daughter when she visits.
